stem: An electronics testing study measures the battery life (hours) for a sample of 20 smartphone models. The sample mean is 9.3 hours with a sample standard deviation of 2.4 hours. However, 3 of the 20 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 17 observations have a mean of 8.6 hours and standard deviation of 1.5 hours. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 9.3, 95% CI = [8.2, 10.4]. Without outliers: mean = 8.6, 95% CI = [7.9, 9.3]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [7.9, 10.4]. Point estimate: 8.9 hours.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [7.9, 10.4].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
